newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-LASORDA IN GOOD CONDITION AFTER SECOND ANGIOPLASTY.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-LASORDA IN GOOD CONDITION AFTER SECOND ANGIOPLASTY.

text.p: Former Los Angeles Dodgers manager Tommy Lasorda Friday night underwent his second angioplasty operation in less than four months after complaining of chest pains.
Lasorda, 69, was listed in good condition following surgery at Centinela Hospital Medical Centre. His cardiologist, Dr. Anthony Reid, said he had suffered no damage to his heart.
Lasorda, who retired in July after nearly 20 years as the Dodgers' manager, was admitted to the hospital Friday. Tests showed the clogged artery cleared in a June 26 operation had closed again.

Doctors repeated the procedure. "The result was excellent," Reid said. "He's awake and alert and watching TV." Lasorda was expected to be released sometime over the weekend, most likely Sunday, he said.

Reid said 25 to 30 percent of all patients who undergo angioplasty -- involving the insertion of a balloon-like catheter into an artery which is then inflated to remove blockage -- require a repeat of the procedure within a year.
Lasorda first entered the hospital in June complaining of abdominal pains, and tests revealed he had suffered a mild heart attack. The first angioplasty was performed two days later.
Lasorda led the Dodgers to two World Series titles and gained a reputation as one of baseball's most colourful characters. After his retirement, he was named a team vice president.

Lasorda spent 47 years with the Dodgers organisation -- as a player, scout, coach and, beginning in 1976, as manager. He was voted National League Manager of the Year three times, in 1977, 1981 and 1988.
